name: PetMed Express, Inc.
business_overview: PetMed Express, Inc., together with its subsidiaries, operates as a pet pharmacy in the United States. The company markets prescription and non-prescription pet medications, health products, and other supplies for dogs, cats, and horses. It offers non-prescription medications and supplies, such as flea and tick control products, bone and joint care products, vitamins, treats, nutritional supplements, hygiene products, and household pet supplies; and prescription medications, including heartworm preventatives, flea and tick preventatives, arthritis, dermatitis, thyroid, diabetes, pain medications, heart/blood pressure, and other specialty medications, as well as generic substitutes. The company also sells food, beds, crates, stairs, and other pet supplies. It sells its products through its Internet website; mobile app; customer support center; and direct mail/print, which includes brochures and postcards. The company was incorporated in 1996 and is headquartered in Delray Beach, Florida.

classification_meta.logic_summary: Pet pharmacy retailing medications and supplies online and via mail order.

narrative.text:
**Business & market dynamics:** PetMed Express is stabilizing with sequential net sales improvement and a narrowing loss, benefiting from strengthening pet telehealth and e-commerce demand. The core pharmacy business is leveraging new white-label and B2B channels, highlighted by a first large-scale partnership with Rural King, which expands its digital footprint and customer access. Despite this, top-line pressure persists, with revenue still declining year-on-year, reflecting ongoing competitive or demand challenges in the pet medication market.

**Management strategy and execution:** Leadership is executing a turnaround centered on a leaner cost structure and diversification through white-label pharmacy services, using existing infrastructure to support retail partners. The Rural King deal signals a strategic pivot toward scalable B2B revenue, and management points to improving sequential performance as evidence of traction. Market credibility is cautiously improving. Note: The input erroneously includes articles about the unrelated UK firm Pets at Home Group (LSE:PETS), creating confusion; the narrative here is based solely on PetMed Express (Nasdaq:PETS) coverage.
